title: Scene compatibility gate for topic-first historical palindrome generation
purpose: Prevent broad-field matches such as 秋・月 from admitting scene-incompatible factor swaps before human review.

evidence_tiers.use: May approve a factor combination despite missing structured scene tags; still does not prove classical correctness.
May support automatic scene overlap when a non-generic scene tag is shared.
Insufficient by itself for automatic crossover.

prerequisites: all five phrases historically attested in the fixed-50 baseline
B/D seam gate complete and nonblocked
gate_v1.automatic_pass: Imported factor shares at least one non-generic scene-specific tag with the core scene.
gate_v1.review_pass: If automatic_pass fails, prior or new human semantic review explicitly approves scene coherence.
gate_v1.hold: If neither automatic_pass nor review_pass is satisfied.
gate_v1.note: The gate filters research candidates; it does not certify grammar or historical-Japanese naturalness.

case_studies.lesson: When structured tags are sparse, human factor-level semantic review can preserve a promising family without pretending the tags are richer than the source data.
All three novel outputs pass palindrome/local-factor/seam constraints but share only generic 月/秋-level semantics with the core; none reached strong/promising status in v0.40.

design_consequences: Do not use broad_field alone as a generation gate.
Store scene tags at factor or phrase level where evidence permits, rather than inheriting all source-level tags blindly.
Generic tags such as 月 and 秋 should not count as scene-specific compatibility by themselves.
Missing scene metadata is not evidence of incompatibility; it triggers human review rather than rejection.
Human semantic approval and source-image/grammar verification remain separate axes.
next_data_work: Add factor-level scene signatures only where v0.40 or source text supports them.
Test the gate on a second positive family outside the はに corridor before enforcing it globally.
Do not rewrite v0.42 scores until the gate has more than the current two-family evidence base.
